title: A New Fossil Hints at the Surprising Origins of Snakes - Nautilus
gist: A Nature study describes Tametara mirim, an exceptionally preserved Cretaceous snake ancestor from Brazil, whose skull anatomy suggests a burrowing lifestyle, informing the debate on snake origins.

insights.claim: A Cretaceous fossil found in 2020 west of São Paulo, Brazil, was described in Nature as a new early snake ancestor species, Tametara mirim, about the length of the bottom of a coat hanger.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: New fossil evidence adds to a long-running debate on whether snakes evolved in the sea, underground or on land.
insights.locator: A study recently published in the journal Nature

insights.claim: Based on its skull anatomy, the authors suggested Tametara mirim led a burrowing lifestyle.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Supports a burrowing-origin hypothesis for snakes.
